title: Gale's feasibility theorem, the Gale–Ryser theorem and Hoffman's circulation theorem
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of D. Gale, A theorem on flows in networks (Pacific J. Math. 7, 1957) and of Hoffman's circulation theorem (A. J. Hoffman, 1960, in the form of A. Schrijver, A Course in Combinatorial Optimization, Theorems 4.6 and 4.7). A network is a finite node type N with capacities c : N → N → ℝ, c ≥ 0 (finite capacities only); a flow is f : N → N → ℝ with f x y + f y x = 0 and f ≤ c; a demand d : N → ℝ is feasible if some flow has net inflow ∑_y f y x ≥ d x at every node. feasibility: d is feasible if and only if d(Sᶜ) ≤ c(S, Sᶜ) for every S ⊆ N (Gale's Feasibility Theorem). feasibility_int: the same for integer c and d with an integer flow (Gale's remark). feasibility_second: Gale's second formulation (for every set Y of nodes of positive demand, some flow meets the demand at all nodes of nonpositive demand and the aggregate demand of Y). gale_ryser_unsorted, gale_ryser: for a : Fin m → ℕ and b : Fin n → ℕ, a 0-1 matrix with row sums at most a i and column sums b j exists if and only if ∑_{j∈Y} b j ≤ ∑_i min(a i, |Y|) for all column sets Y, equivalently, for b nonincreasing, ∑_{j<k} b j ≤ ∑_{j<k} #{i | j < a i} for all k ≤ n (Gale's Problem I, §3). gale_ryser_exact: if moreover ∑ a = ∑ b, the row sums can be made exactly a (the Gale–Ryser theorem). hoffman, hoffman_int: on a finite directed multigraph (arc type A, tail and head maps src, tgt : A → V) with bounds d ≤ c on the arcs (real, respectively integer), there is a circulation f (real, respectively integer) with d ≤ f ≤ c if and only if d(δ^in(U)) ≤ c(δ^out(U)) for every U ⊆ V. Eight statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
